q: What crisis wakes the boys on the morning of day five?
a: Karuizawa's underwear has gone missing from the luggage piled outside the tents overnight; she is crying while Kushida comforts her.

q: How do the girls initially respond to the theft?
a: They presume a boy did it, demand the boys' bags be searched, and Shinohara treats the class as harboring an underwear thief.

q: How does Hirata defuse the bag-search standoff?
a: He volunteers to open his own luggage first, shaming everyone into compliance so no refuser becomes suspect.

q: What is found in Ike's bag, and why is Ayanokouji skeptical he's guilty?
a: Karuizawa's white underwear - but Ayanokouji reasons no thief would hide stolen goods in his own bag before an inevitable search, and Ike showed no panic when told to open it; someone planted it.

q: How does the evidence end up in Ayanokouji's pocket?
a: Panicking, Ike thrusts the balled underwear into Ayanokouji's hands to hide; with no time or place, Ayanokouji stuffs it into his back pocket.

q: How does Hirata cover for Ayanokouji during the pat-down?
a: Feeling the underwear in his back pocket, Hirata locks eyes with him, then announces 'Ayanokouji-kun doesn't have them either,' ending the search on his credible word.

q: Why does Hirata insist on holding the underwear himself?
a: Like holding the Joker - if anyone must be branded culprit, as Karuizawa's boyfriend he would take the least damage; he seals it in a vinyl toilet bag.

q: What contradictory request does Hirata make of Ayanokouji afterward?
a: To hunt the real culprit but report only to him first and keep it secret - even concealing the truth if a boy turns out guilty - which Ayanokouji reads as both lifeline and warning from a man who half-suspects him.

q: What punitive separation do the girls impose?
a: A drawn border bans boys from the girls' side, boys must relocate their tent without help, and they are barred from the shower until the culprit is found.

q: Whom does Horikita propose as the second trusted helper beside Hirata, and on what logic?
a: Ayanokouji - not from trust, which she disclaims entirely, but by process of elimination as the only boy whose exclusion she cannot justify and who can watch Hirata's back.

q: How does Karuizawa humiliate Sakura during the meeting?
a: After Sakura timidly defends Ayanokouji, Karuizawa teases that Sakura must like him and demands a public confession until Sakura flees in tears into the forest, chased by Kushida.

q: Why does suspicion shift to Ibuki?
a: With boys cleared by inspection, someone mutters that Class C outsider Ibuki could be sabotaging them, and the collective's doubt pivots to this new prey.

q: What conclusion about the theft's timing does Ayanokouji reach?
a: The crime happened between 8 PM and 7 AM, almost certainly around sunrise after five o'clock - a flashlight raid at deep night would have woken someone.

q: Why does Ibuki approach Ayanokouji about the case?
a: Knowing she'll be the next suspect once boys are cleared, she probes whether he doubts her; he answers honestly that he trusts she isn't the culprit - though internally he concludes she stole and planted it, noting dirt under her nails.

q: What secret spending does Horikita expose inside the girls' tent?
a: Floor mats, air-inflated pillows, and battery-powered cordless fans in both tents - twelve points of comfort Karuizawa's group ordered quietly, which Hirata knew of via report but never shared.

q: How does Ayanokouji prove Horikita is running a fever?
a: He lists the evidence - disheveled bangs from lying down, chills on the hot deck, long zipped sleeves - then touches her forehead, finding nearly 38 degrees Celsius.

q: Why does Horikita hide her illness despite the stakes?
a: Reporting it would trigger the thirty-point retirement penalty against the class, more than Karuizawa's splurging cost; she vows to endure a few more days.

q: What embarrassing thing does a sleeping Sudou do to Ayanokouji?
a: Pinning him with his legs and moaning 'Suzune…I can't hold back anymore…' before Ayanokouji shrieks free.

q: Why does Kushida join the food-search group on day six?
a: Officially her friends are caring for Mii-chan's period cramps; really she wants a chance to finally talk with the Horikita who dislikes her.

q: What observation does Kushida make about Ayanokouji and Horikita?
a: That neither ever genuinely smiles - she has never seen either laugh from the heart, suggesting they share that in common.

q: What prank does Ayanokouji orchestrate with Yamauchi?
a: He bribes Yamauchi with Sakura's email address to smear mud over sick Horikita's hair - creating cover for a staged key-card fumble; Horikita retaliates by throwing Yamauchi.

q: When does Horikita realize her key card was stolen?
a: While changing to wash the mud off in the river - the card vanished from her coat during that interval, and she confesses it to Ayanokouji in the forest, mortified.

q: Which two suspects does Horikita name for the card theft, and how is one eliminated?
a: Karuizawa out of hatred, or Ibuki; Karuizawa is alibied because she stood in the shower line the whole time with her flunkies, leaving Ibuki prime suspect given the morning's timing.

q: What second disaster strikes behind the temporary toilet?
a: Someone burns the class manual - paper scavenged as kindling - just as heavy rain arrives, and Hirata, owner of the bag it came from, crushes a water bottle muttering 'It's just like back then.'

q: Who disappears amid the fire chaos?
a: Ibuki - along with one of the bags - making her the obvious arson suspect in everyone's eyes.

q: Whose point of view narrates the rainy chase after the card thief?
a: Horikita's - feverish, she pursues the thief alone through the storm, repeating that she must make up for her mistake.

q: How does the thief bait Horikita into an inadvertent confession?
a: Asked to return 'what you took from me,' the thief replies about the keycard - which Horikita never named - exposing that she knows exactly what was stolen before catching herself.

q: Describe the fight between Horikita and the card thief.
a: A feinted punch into a high kick opens; Horikita is seized and thrown, escapes via martial-arts rolls, lands a solar-plexus counter at the edge of collapse, but her fever saps her - the skilled, smiling thief overpowers her, slaps her, kicks her face, and reveals the card bearing Horikita's own name.

q: What does the thief deny, and what tantalizing hint does she drop?
a: She denies burning the manual - nothing to gain, everything to lose - and taunts that some guy figured her out before Horikita did, right before a blunt instrument knocks Horikita unconscious and a voice says 'This conversation is over.'

q: What was Ibuki's original plan for proving the leader's identity?
a: To photograph the keycard with her digital camera as irrefutable evidence - but the camera broke, forcing her to physically steal the card.

q: How was Ibuki's infiltration of Class D engineered?
a: Ryuuen slapped her to turn a lie into truth - the real injury made Class D believe she'd been beaten and exiled for defiance.

q: Who verifies the stolen card, and what leverage secures his cooperation?
a: Katsuragi, whose condition was proof; Ryuuen leverages rumors that Sakayanagi's faction is ascendant ever since Katsuragi failed to enter the student council, framing alliance as his chance - Katsuragi shakes hands.

q: What secret pact do Ryuuen and Katsuragi conclude?
a: An A-C alliance: details unspoken but promising huge returns - later revealed as Class C buying whatever Class A needed so A could spend none of its points all week.

q: How does Ibuki dispose of the evidence after the deal?
a: She carefully wipes her fingerprints from the keycard and slips it back into the unconscious Horikita's hand, judging the feverish loner too broken to be a threat.

q: What does Ayanokouji find when he tracks the footprints?
a: Horikita collapsed unconscious beside the returned keycard, soil showing something had been excavated nearby - proof more people than Ibuki now knew the leader's identity.

q: What harsh self-diagnosis does a waking Horikita make?
a: That she could have avoided everything if she knew how to rely on people - muttering 'I'm so pathetic' since having no friends left her guarding the card alone.

q: What offer does Ayanokouji make as he embraces the feverish Horikita?
a: 'If you can't fight by yourself, it's better to fight with a partner. I'll lend you a hand.'

q: What slip does Horikita make while begging Ayanokouji to leave her behind?
a: She says 'Because I think of you as my friend, please listen to my request' - then covers her mouth in surprise at her own words.

q: What ruthless inner monologue does Ayanokouji have while holding Horikita?
a: That he never thought of her as a friend or classmate - winning is everything, all people including Hirata are tools, and she shouldn't blame herself because she was useful to him.

q: How does Ayanokouji get Horikita off the island?
a: He carries her through the storm, reaches the ship's ramp at 7:58 - two minutes before roll call - invokes the emergency, and has a stretcher take her aboard as a health retirement.

q: What final costs does Ayanokouji tally for Class D that night?
a: Thirty points for Horikita's retirement plus five for his own absence at evening roll call.

q: In what order and with what totals are the island test rankings announced?
a: Fourth/last: Class C with zero; third: Class A with 120; second: Class B with 140; and first place: Class D with 225 points.

q: Why does Ryuuen remain on the beach when results are read?
a: He never retired - he was the lone Class C student left controlling the operation; tanned classmates had all withdrawn to the ship by day two.

q: How does Ryuuen needle Sudou at the results gathering?
a: By calling Horikita 'Suzune' twice, boasting they were together before, tossing his crushed cup for Sudou to discard, and musing about squeezing her bottom - until Sudou seizes his collar.

q: What claim makes Class D's victory seem impossible beforehand?
a: Ryuuen announced he had written Class D's leader's name on his answer sheet - and Classes A and B wrote the same - implying D should suffer massive exposure penalties.

q: Why did all three rival classes' guesses fail?
a: Every class guessed Horikita Suzune - but after her retirement, Ayanokouji Kiyotaka had been appointed replacement leader under the rule that retirement counts as suitable justification for a change, so all guesses were wrong and each guessing class forfeited fifty points and its bonuses.

q: How do Class A students react to finishing third?
a: They swarm Katsuragi demanding to know the meaning of it while he can only mutter that something is strange.

q: What state is Kouenji in when Class D boards the ship?
a: Perfectly tanned and glossy-skinned with a drink in hand, claiming poor health forced his rest - drawing unified yelling over his thirty-point penalty.

q: How does Horikita handle being called 'Suzune' by Sudou post-test?
a: She accepts it naturally for a moment - then forbids him from using her first name without permission, leaving him nodding meekly.

q: What apology does Karuizawa give Horikita, and what cover story accompanies it?
a: She apologizes for the theft accusations, explaining Ibuki stole the underwear and that Horikita collapsed chasing her - and credits Horikita with identifying Class A and C's leaders, the sanctioned explanation for their win that leaves Horikita bewildered.

q: How does Chabashira invert the Icarus myth in her debrief?
a: She notes Icarus flew on wings his father built and directed - like Ayanokouji acting on another's design - and quotes his father: 'Sooner or later, Kiyotaka will gladly chase the means of his expulsion from school'; Ayanokouji replies that Icarus won't heed Daedalus' warnings.

q: What hints did the school plant about spot locations?
a: The ship's unusually fast full circuit of the island, the odd announcement calling it 'significant scenery,' and visible man-made paths - which Katsuragi exploited and Kouenji also noticed.

q: Why was the cave the most strategically valuable spot?
a: Not for itself but its location - no spots sat near the river or well, yet two others (the cliff hut and the lookout tower) lay near the cave, letting its holder control the area.

q: Why was Katsuragi holding Yahiko's key card at the cave?
a: Insurance - cautious Katsuragi would never occupy immediately, so when short-sightedly greedy Yahiko carelessly did, Katsuragi displayed the card to misdirect any witness into naming him leader.

q: How does Ayanokouji explain Class A's fatal carelessness?
a: Internal schism: Katsuragi couldn't rely on Sakayanagi-faction classmates, so no sentries watched the cave - their apparent perfection hid a huge rift.

q: What proved Ryuuen was still on the island directing operations?
a: Ibuki buried a wireless transceiver to contact him - equipment retired students shouldn't possess - meaning someone remained to receive her signals; Ryuuen ran the transceiver alone, trusting no one.

q: Why did Ibuki need photographic evidence rather than word of mouth?
a: Because parties beyond Class C wouldn't trust her testimony alone - the camera photo of the keycard was meant as proof for the A-C deal.

q: What hidden alliance explains Class A finishing with 270 unspent?
a: Classes A and C secretly cooperated: C sacrificed its own points buying everything A needed, letting A hoard all 300 (reduced to 270 by the illness penalty) without spending a point.

q: What habit betrayed Ibuki's lies to Ayanokouji?
a: She holds eye contact while lying - the opposite of the guilty norm - deliberately, perhaps unconsciously, to sell falsehoods as truth.

q: What physical token does Ayanokouji reveal to Horikita in the lounge?
a: His new key card engraved 'Ayanokouji Kiyotaka' - documentary proof he became Class D's leader upon her retirement.

q: What one condition does Ayanokouji set for helping Horikita reach Class A?
a: That she never investigate his past or touch the subject again; she accepts without hesitation, saying some things are better left buried.

q: How does Volume 3 end?
a: With a firm handshake and parallel resolve - 'I work for me. You do things for yourself.' - as the battle to raise Class D from the bottom begins.
